get.description: Public because a username is a public identifier — confirming one is taken reveals nothing a profile page would not. Rate limited, because an instant public answer is also a way to harvest the handles in use.
get.summary: Check whether a username is free

post.description: Creates no account. The sign-up waits, and a six-digit code is emailed to the address; the account is created only when that code is confirmed. Answers 202 whether or not the address already has an account, so the endpoint cannot be used to discover which addresses do — the owner of an existing account is told by email instead. Signing up again at an address that is still waiting replaces the waiting details and sends a new code. A taken username answers 409, including one held by a sign-up still waiting for confirmation.
Answers 202 for an unknown address, an existing account and a waiting sign-up alike. Only a sign-up still waiting is sent a code, and the new code replaces the previous one.

Creates the account from the waiting sign-up. Wrong, expired and unknown all answer the same 400, and five wrong guesses retire the code. Does not sign the person in: they sign in with their email address and password, which keeps a forwarded code from becoming a session. Limited per address as well as per IP, so rotating IPs buys no extra guesses.
post.summary: Confirm the address and create the account

post.description: Emails a six-digit recovery code. An address whose sign-up was never confirmed has no password to reset, and is sent a reminder to sign up again instead. Answers 202 for every address, known or not: a reset endpoint that only responds for real accounts is a membership oracle that needs no password to query.

Returns a single-use token, valid for ten minutes, that `reset` accepts. Wrong, expired and unknown all answer the same 400. Limited per address as well as per IP, because the code belongs to an account and the guessing budget has to be spent per account too.
post.summary: Exchange a recovery code for a reset grant

post.description: Ends every existing session. Someone resetting a password is often doing it because they believe the account is compromised; leaving the attacker signed in would defeat the exercise.
Requires the current password. Ends every session on every device, including this one, and returns a fresh token pair so the caller stays signed in where they are.
post.summary: Change the password of the signed-in user
